prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Across the five frames, the depth map tracks the camera wearer tilting their head up from the ground (frames 1–3) toward an outdoor horizon with a car, two standing people, and distant hills (frames 4–5). It reveals spatial structures hidden by heavy darkness and backlighting in the RGB strip, specifically a person's legs standing ~1.5–2 m ahead in frame 1, the camera wearer's own left hand (~0.3–0.5 m, within arm's reach at the bottom-left) in frame 3, and the layered arrangement in frame 5 where the wearer's raised right hand holding a loop (~0.3–0.5 m, bottom-right) partially occludes a nearer person (~1.5–2 m away, slightly left of center) and a car with an open trunk (~1.5–2.5 m away on the left). In frame 5, the depth map also distinguishes a second person standing ~3–4 m away to the right (~1.5–2 m behind and to the right of the nearer person), with the nearer person facing right toward the car/second person and the farther person facing left in profile rather than looking at the camera wearer. Over frames 4 to 5, as the camera turns upward and rightward, the car and nearer person remain within reach of each other while the wearer's right hand rises into the immediate foreground. However, the depth map is unreliable in the pitch-black regions of frames 2 and 3—producing smooth, featureless or inverted gradients at the upper left—and in frame 5 it merges the nearer person and the open car trunk into a single bright mass without clear object boundaries.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map fails to capture almost the entire scene layout across the five frames due to extreme underexposure in frames 1–3 and strong backlighting in frames 4–5, leaving the ground, sky, hills, and vehicle completely unsegmented. Its only accurate detection occurs in frame 5, where it segments the upper body of the farther person standing ~3–4 m away on the right (who faces left toward the car and away from the camera wearer's line of sight, with their lower legs cut off in the mask), providing a clearer torso and arm boundary against the dark ground than the silhouetted RGB image. In frame 2, the map is unreliable because it misclassifies a small glowing red-and-green indicator near the ground (~1 m ahead, slightly left of center) as a 'traffic light'. Furthermore, across the sequence as the camera tilts up from the ground toward the horizon, segmentation completely misses the person's legs in frame 1 (~1.5–2 m away), the car (~1.5–2.5 m away on the left in frames 4–5), and the nearer standing person (~1.5–2 m away, ~1.5–2 m in front of and to the left of the segmented person in frame 5) who is within arm's reach of the car. It also fails to detect the camera wearer's own hands and held object entering within arm's reach (~0.3–0.5 m) at the bottom of frames 3 and 5, offering no information on foreground occlusions.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is blank in frames 1, 2, 4, and 5, detecting only a single magenta hand skeleton at the bottom-left of frame 3 as the camera wearer's left hand rises into view within arm's reach (~0.3–0.5 m in front of and below the camera). This skeleton clearly shows the palm and curled finger joints angled upward and to the right, which is difficult to discern in the heavily underexposed RGB frame where the lower arm is partly out of view below the bottom edge. As the camera tilts up and turns slightly right across frames 4 and 5 toward the outdoor scene with the car (~1.5–2.5 m on the left) and hills, the pose map is highly unreliable because it fails to track the wearer's left hand leaving the view or the wearer's right hand (~0.3–0.5 m at the bottom-right in frame 5) holding an object that partially occludes the mid-ground. It also completely misses the full-body and hand skeletons of the person standing ~1.5–2 m ahead in frame 1 and both people in frames 4–5—the nearer person at ~1.5–2 m facing right alongside the car and the farther person ~3–4 m away on the right (~1.5–2 m behind the first) facing left—leaving their facing directions, gaze away from the camera wearer, and reach relative to the car unrepresented.
